label: M4 S1 | The Three Golden Integrity Equations

formulas.name: The Balance Sheet Identity
formulas.formula: Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity

variables.meaning: Everything the company owns — cash, receivables, inventory, PP&E, intangibles
Everything the company owes — payables, debt, deferred tax, provisions
Shareholders' residual claim — share capital + reserves + retained earnings

formulas.worked_example: Titan FY24: Total Assets = ₹23,512 cr. Total Liabilities = ₹14,890 cr. Total Equity = ₹8,622 cr. Check: 14,890 + 8,622 = 23,512. ✓ Balanced. In your model, you will build a cell that computes Assets − (Liabilities + Equity). If it is ever anything other than zero (or a rounding difference below ₹0.01 cr), your model is broken. This single cell, at the top of your Balance Sheet tab, is the most important formula in the entire workbook.
formulas.sensitivity_note: If the balance sheet does not balance, do not proceed. Do not forecast the next year. Do not start the DCF. Fix it first. 95% of the time the error is in the Cash Flow Statement linkage — a missing item in CFO, a sign error in capex, or a debt movement that was not flowed through.

formulas.name: The Cash Flow Reconciliation
formulas.formula: Closing Cash = Opening Cash + CFO + CFI + CFF

variables.meaning: Cash balance at the start of the period, pulled from prior year BS
Cash Flow from Operations — cash generated by running the business
Cash Flow from Investing — cash spent on capex, acquisitions, investments
Cash Flow from Financing — cash from debt issuance, equity, less dividends and repayments

formulas.worked_example: Titan FY24: Opening Cash ₹1,240 cr + CFO ₹2,860 cr + CFI (−₹1,920 cr) + CFF (−₹380 cr) = Closing Cash ₹1,800 cr. The Closing Cash figure must equal the Cash line on the Balance Sheet at year-end. If it doesn't, your statements are disconnected — which means your model is lying.
formulas.sensitivity_note: This is the second integrity check. Build a cell that computes (CFS Closing Cash − BS Cash). It must be zero. If it isn't, you have a linkage error — usually a missing item in CFO (like a non-cash expense you forgot to add back) or a double-counted item in CFF.

formulas.name: The Retained Earnings Roll
formulas.formula: Closing Retained Earnings = Opening Retained Earnings + Net Income − Dividends

variables.meaning: Prior year closing RE from the BS
Bottom line of the IS for the current year
Cash paid to shareholders, pulled from CFF

formulas.worked_example: Titan FY24: Opening RE ₹7,100 cr + Net Income ₹3,496 cr − Dividends ₹1,510 cr = Closing RE ₹9,086 cr. This closing figure flows directly into the Equity section of the current year Balance Sheet. If you break this link, retained earnings will not grow correctly, and the BS will not balance.
formulas.sensitivity_note: This is the third integrity check and the one most often broken by beginners. The mistake is usually either forgetting to link dividends from CFF into the RE roll, or linking Net Income to the wrong year. Always trace the formula: RE_current = RE_prior + NI_current − Dividends_current.

formulas.name: The Balance Sheet Identity
formulas.formula: Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity

variables.meaning: Everything the company owns — cash, receivables, inventory, PP&E, intangibles
Everything the company owes — payables, debt, deferred tax, provisions
Shareholders' residual claim — share capital + reserves + retained earnings

formulas.plain_english: Every rupee of assets must come from either debt (liabilities) or shareholder money (equity). This is not a formula to calculate something new — it is a law of accounting. If your balance sheet does not balance, your model has an error. Think of it as the heartbeat monitor of your financial model: if it flatlines, the model is dead.
computation: Sum all asset line items (current and non-current)
Sum all liability line items (current and non-current)
Sum all equity line items (share capital, reserves, retained earnings)
Compare to Total Assets — must be equal (within rounding)

worked_example.problem: Titan's FY24 balance sheet shows Total Assets of ₹23,512 cr. Total Liabilities are ₹14,890 cr. Verify the balance sheet identity.
steps: Add Total Liabilities + Total Equity = ₹14,890 cr + ₹8,622 cr = ₹23,512 cr
worked_example.insight: In your Excel model, build a cell at the top of the Balance Sheet tab that computes Assets − (Liabilities + Equity). If it ever shows anything other than zero (or a rounding difference below ₹0.01 cr), your model is broken. Do not forecast. Do not build the DCF. Fix the error first. 95% of the time the culprit is a missing item in the Cash Flow Statement linkage — a sign error in capex, a non-cash add-back you forgot, or a debt movement that never flowed through to cash.

formulas.sensitivity_note: If the balance sheet does not balance, do not proceed. Do not forecast the next year. Do not start the DCF. Fix it first. 95% of the time the error is in the Cash Flow Statement linkage — a missing item in CFO, a sign error in capex, or a debt movement that was not flowed through.

formulas.name: The Cash Flow Reconciliation
formulas.formula: Closing Cash = Opening Cash + CFO + CFI + CFF

variables.meaning: Cash balance at the start of the period, pulled from prior year BS
Cash Flow from Operations — cash generated by running the business
Cash Flow from Investing — cash spent on capex, acquisitions, investments
Cash Flow from Financing — cash from debt issuance, equity, less dividends and repayments

formulas.plain_english: Your cash flow statement must reconcile to your balance sheet. Starting with last year's cash, you add the cash generated from operations, subtract the cash spent on capex and acquisitions, and adjust for borrowings and dividends. The result must equal this year's cash balance on the balance sheet. If it doesn't, your P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow are not connected — which means your model is internally inconsistent and unusable for forecasting.
computation: Pull Opening Cash from prior year Balance Sheet (Cash line)
Add or subtract CFI (negative if capex and acquisitions exceed investment returns)
Add or subtract CFF (negative if dividends and debt repayment exceed new borrowing)
Compute the sum — this is Closing Cash
Verify that Closing Cash equals the Cash line on the current year Balance Sheet

worked_example.problem: Titan's FY24 cash flow statement shows: Opening Cash ₹1,240 cr, CFO ₹2,860 cr, CFI of −₹1,920 cr, and CFF of −₹380 cr. What should Closing Cash be, and how does it link to the balance sheet?
steps: Verify: Cash on Balance Sheet = ₹1,800 cr ✓
worked_example.result: Closing Cash = ₹1,800 cr, matching the Balance Sheet.
worked_example.insight: This is your second integrity check. Build a cell in your model that computes (CFS Closing Cash − BS Cash). It must equal zero. If it doesn't, you have a linkage error — usually a missing non-cash add-back in CFO (e.g., depreciation you forgot to add back to net income) or a double-counted item in CFF. Trace the error before proceeding to valuation.

formulas.sensitivity_note: This is the second integrity check. Build a cell that computes (CFS Closing Cash − BS Cash). It must be zero. If it isn't, you have a linkage error — usually a missing item in CFO (like a non-cash expense you forgot to add back) or a double-counted item in CFF.

formulas.name: The Retained Earnings Roll
formulas.formula: Closing Retained Earnings = Opening Retained Earnings + Net Income − Dividends

variables.meaning: Prior year closing RE from the BS
Bottom line of the IS for the current year
Cash paid to shareholders, pulled from CFF

formulas.plain_english: Retained earnings is how much profit the company has accumulated since inception, less any dividends paid out. Each year, you start with last year's retained earnings, add the profit earned this year, and subtract the cash returned to shareholders. The result flows into the equity section of the balance sheet. Break this link and the equity side will not reconcile — your balance sheet will fail the integrity test.
computation: Pull Opening Retained Earnings from prior year Balance Sheet (Equity section)
Add Net Income from the current year Income Statement
Subtract Dividends Paid (from the Cash Flow Statement, CFF section)
The result is Closing Retained Earnings
Verify that this closing RE value appears in the current year Balance Sheet under Equity

worked_example.problem: Titan's FY24 shows Opening RE of ₹7,100 cr, Net Income of ₹3,496 cr, and Dividends of ₹1,510 cr. Calculate closing RE and verify it flows to the balance sheet.
steps: Add Net Income: ₹7,100 cr + ₹3,496 cr = ₹10,596 cr
Verify: This ₹9,086 cr appears on the Balance Sheet in the Equity section ✓
worked_example.result: Closing Retained Earnings = ₹9,086 cr, correctly linked to Balance Sheet equity.
worked_example.insight: This is the third integrity check and the one most often broken by analysts building their first model. The two most common mistakes: (1) forgetting to link dividends from the Cash Flow Statement into the RE roll, so equity grows too fast; (2) linking Net Income to the wrong year (e.g., using prior year NI instead of current year), causing retained earnings to be out of sync. Always trace the formula in your model: RE_current = RE_prior + NI_current − Dividends_current. Use cell references, not numbers.

formulas.sensitivity_note: This is the third integrity check and the one most often broken by beginners. The mistake is usually either forgetting to link dividends from CFF into the RE roll, or linking Net Income to the wrong year. Always trace the formula: RE_current = RE_prior + NI_current − Dividends_current.
